findings.note: parent_not_active remedy differs by role: captain asks its officer (L1-025), admiral dispatches the captain's crew (L2-023), chief of staff asks the user (L2-213), standard gives none (L6-063). Only a gap if a captain with no invoked admiral is read as "the user" in both L1-025 and L2-023.
L1-016 "preserving the fresh reviewer obligation" and "open native capacity" are used without a definition or a measure of how capacity is budgeted (L1-016, L2-018, L6-052).
Probe timeout is "short" in L1-029, L1-030, L3-051, L4-020 but 120 s in L3-174; no statement defines "short". The reviewer cap (4G/120) and crew probe cap (4G/short) may differ.
L1-029 requires "a gate lock outside the cap" without any statement defining the gate lock.

The 110k context limit appears in the commission (L1-210, L2-336) and is stated by the brief (L4-065, L1-250), but no statement says what happens when the swarm width or Codex cap changes mid-run beyond L1-231 handing a finished share back.
L2-223 refers to "these three lists" that no statement of this group defines; the rule is stated only in the chief-of-staff skill, where the lists sit.
L2-292 is stated only in the night-survey resource that the surveyor reads, not where the chief of staff acts; the chief of staff never reads it as an instruction to itself.
L6-064 is stated only in the working-tree standard; the ticket-captain skill (L1-020..L1-025) never says a native captain cannot reach a Codex reviewer.
L7-058 (docs-writer for a documentation change) overlaps L1-079 and L1-013; the statements sit in different claims because they differ in scope (one author per ticket vs documentation routing).
L2-163 defines a failed or lost survey as not running for the admiral; L2-245 says "pending" for the chief of staff with no statement saying a failed or lost night survey is not pending.
L4-002 (inquisitor skill) omits the proof branch name, test paths and the Break n counter that L1-250 requires of the brief; the inquisitor cannot check a brief against its own skill.

L1-046 and L2-073 require HITL in a new top-level thread while L1-035, L2-026, L2-214 forbid top-level threads for crew; consistent only because of the HITL exception, which L1-035/L2-026/L2-214 each restate.
L4-072 and L4-073 do not say what happens at exactly the limit (L4-018 says "past").
